prompt:
The graph below shows the average amount of fine dust measured in the air of three cities between 2005 and 2025.

Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.
instruction_line: You should spend about 20 minutes on this task. Write at least 150 words.

visual.title: Fine dust in the air of three cities, 2005-2025
visual.alt: Line chart showing changes in fine dust levels in the air of three cities between 2005 and 2025, in micrograms per cubic metre.

key_points: Dust levels fall continuously in Ashport and Corley: Ashport drops from 62 to 26 (roughly two-thirds), and Corley falls from 48 to 28.
Bellworth moves in the opposite direction; it rises from 30 to 46 in 2020, then falls back slightly to 42 — this is the only peak.
The ranking completely reverses: in 2005 Bellworth had the cleanest air and Ashport the most polluted; by 2025 Bellworth has the highest value and Ashport the lowest.
There are two crossovers in the chart: Bellworth overtakes Corley between 2010 and 2015, then overtakes Ashport between 2015 and 2020.
Ashport's decline is of similar size in each five-year period (7-11 units) and continuous; Corley's main fall only begins after 2010.
By 2025, Ashport and Corley are very close to each other (26 and 28), but Bellworth remains at roughly one and a half times the level of either.
common_mistakes: Missing the two crossovers and the reversal in ranking — this is the chart's main story.
Giving an opinion or inventing a cause ('Bellworth should limit traffic in the city centre')
Describing the three cities separately without making any comparison between them.
Dropping the unit or mistaking it for a percentage ('dust fell by 26%')
Ignoring the small dip in Bellworth after 2020 and presenting the line as continuously rising.
topic: fine dust levels in the air
